fact_standard.quote: the exact sentence from that source, so anyone can check it without re-researching. Null when status is unverifiable — a quote is never fabricated.
fact_standard.source: a primary source where possible: the original paper (ISSCC, Hot Chips, MICRO, ISCA), the vendor's manual or datasheet, or the patent. Wikipedia and blogs should only be pointers to those.

status_meanings.corrected: the wiki value was wrong and has been fixed; previous_value keeps the old value
status_meanings.disputed: sources disagree; both are listed in the record's notes
status_meanings.unverifiable: the fact appears only in secondary sources; no primary source could be obtained
status_meanings.verified: the value in the wiki matches the primary source

records.current_value: Complete 4-bit parallel CPU; 1-word instructions are 8 bits requiring 8 clock periods (one instruction cycle), 2-word instructions 16 clock periods; no branch prediction block in the datasheet architecture
records.fact: Building blocks — no branch prediction unit; simple 4-bit CPU with fixed instruction cycle
records.notes: Absence of branch prediction cannot be proved by a single positive sentence; the correction rests on the datasheet's complete architectural description, which lists the accumulator, index registers, pointer stack, instruction encoding/decoder, timing and control — with no prediction or speculative-fetch mechanism — and defines the fixed cycle in the Instruction Set Format section: a 1-word instruction is 8 bits requiring 8 clock periods (instruction cycle) and a 2-word instruction is 16 bits requiring 16 clock periods (2 instruction cycles). Conditional branching exists (JCN), but it is resolved in the normal instruction cycle, not predicted. Datasheet text is via Intel's original document archived at archive.org; OCR in the archived copy is imperfect outside the quoted sentence.
records.previous_value: Fetch + branch prediction listed among its building blocks

records.fact: The program counter has a dedicated incrementing circuit able to increment all 16 bits in a single cycle

records.current_value: Two 4-bit nibble adders with decimal carry adjustment between nibbles
records.fact: The ALU is a pair of binary nibble ALUs with a decimal adjustment, not a byte-wide ALU with a decimal fix-up
records.notes: Level-2 drill-down fact.
records.quote: The two operands, and the carry in, are added as a pair of nibbles. The carry-out from bit3 is adjusted in decimal mode, but only for ADC. So the ALU is not a binary byte-wide ALU with a decimal adjustment, it is a pair of binary nibble ALUs with a decimal adjustment.

records.current_value: Decimal mode: ADC/SBC only; NMOS usefully sets C only

records.notes: Level-2 drill-down fact. The N, V and Z flags are set but do not correspond to a 10's-complement decimal operation.
records.quote: Decimal mode only affects ADC and SBC instructions, and on the NMOS 6502 only usefully sets the C flag.

records.current_value: $99 + $01 (decimal) => $00, Carry = 1

More significantly, Zen 4's L2 BTB is faster: Zen 3 suffered a three cycle penalty when it needed a branch target from its L2 BTB. Zen 4 brings that penalty down to just one cycle.

source.title: AMD's Zen 4 Part 1: Frontend and Execution Engine

records.fact: Op cache delivers 9 ops per cycle, but throughput is limited by the 6-wide renamer downstream

source.title: AMD's Zen 4 Part 1: Frontend and Execution Engine

records.current_value: MOV/zeroing elimination via RAT aliasing + zero bit; 202/224 int registers for speculative results
records.fact: Renamer eliminates MOVs and zeroing idioms via RAT aliasing and a zero bit; 202 of 224 integer registers measured available for speculative results
records.notes: Level-3 record: the 202-register figure is from the same source: 'We measured 202 integer registers (out of 224) available to hold speculative results, which covers 63% of ROB capacity.'
records.quote: Eliminated MOVs can be handled by pointing multiple architectural registers to the same physical one, meaning that no extra physical registers have to be allocated for such MOVs. If the renamer knows a register's value has to be zero, it can remember that by setting a bit in the register alias table instead of allocating a real integer register.

source.title: AMD's Zen 4 Part 1: Frontend and Execution Engine

records.fact: ROB capacity of 320 entries confirmed by a custom test; each ROB entry can hold up to 4 NOPs
records.notes: Level-3 record: independent confirmation of the published 320-entry ROB; the 4-NOP packing is from the same source: 'Zen 4's reorder buffer is also special, because each entry can hold up to 4 NOPs.'
records.quote: We used a custom test with up to 128 integer adds, 128 floating point adds, 40 stores, and 55 branches (in that order) to confirm AMD's published 320 entry ROB capacity.

source.title: AMD's Zen 4 Part 1: Frontend and Execution Engine

records.notes: Level-3 record: the scheduler select primitive; same source also states 'Scheduler and execution pipe layout were not changed from Zen 3.' and 'A scheduling queue potentially has to check every entry every cycle, to see if it's ready to execute.'
records.quote: On the floating point and vector execution side, Zen 3 and Zen 4 retain the large non-scheduling queue found in previous Zen generations, but move from a unified quad-port scheduler to two triple port schedulers.

source.title: AMD's Zen 4 Part 1: Frontend and Execution Engine

records.notes: Level-3 record: same source: 'Zen 4 and Zen 3 seem to have similarly capable L1 predictors, but AMD has dramatically beefed up Zen 4's L2 predictor. ... It can recognize extremely long patterns and has enough storage to perform very well, even with a lot of branches in play.'
records.quote: Like other CPUs in the Zen series, Zen 4's direction predictor has two overriding levels.

source.title: AMD's Zen 4 Part 1: Frontend and Execution Engine

records.current_value: One micro-op through most of the pipeline; split at the execution pipe

records.notes: Level-3 record: underpins the half-select mux primitive; same source: 'I assume they're broken up into two operations after they enter a 256-bit execution pipe, meaning that the instruction is split into two 256-bit halves as late as possible in the pipeline.'
records.quote: Zen 4 partially breaks this tradition, by keeping instructions that work on 512-bit vectors as one micro-op throughout most of the pipeline.

source.title: AMD's Zen 4 Part 1: Frontend and Execution Engine

records.quote: 512-bit stores are an exception to the rule. They're still decoded into two micro-ops, which means they consume two valuable store queue entries.

source.title: AMD's Zen 4 Part 1: Frontend and Execution Engine

records.quote: Zen 2, 3, and 4 all have two 256-bit FMA units and four 256-bit ALUs.

records.notes: Level-3 record: the rename geometry; the 40 physical registers are the 40 ROB entries, underpinning the ROB-as-register-file and RAT primitives.

records.current_value: 20-entry RS; up to 5 micro-ops dispatched per clock; results sent back to dependent RS entries and stored in ROB
records.fact: Dispatch and writeback: micro-ops wait in the 20-entry RS until operands are data-ready and a functional unit is available; up to 5 micro-ops per clock pass from the RS to the execution units, which send result data back to dependent micro-ops in the RS and store the result in the ROB
records.notes: Level-3 record: the dispatch rate and result-forwarding behaviour; underpins the dispatch arbiter, CAM wakeup and mux/demux primitives.
records.quote: Following renaming, the micro-ops wait in a 20-entry reservation station (RS) until all of their operands are data ready and a functional unit is available. As many as 5 micro-ops per clock can pass from the reservation station to the various execution units. These units perform the desired computation and send the result data back to dependent micro-ops in their reservation stations, as well as storing the result in the reorder buffer (ROB).

records.current_value: ROB stores micro-ops in program order; retires up to 3 per clock into RRF; halts retirement on fault/mispredict
records.fact: ROB retire: the ROB stores micro-ops in original program order and retires up to three per clock into the retirement register file (RRF); it examines each completed micro-op for faults or branch mispredictions and halts further retirement on a discontinuity
records.notes: Level-3 record: the in-order retirement behaviour; underpins the retire-head comparator and retirement-controller primitives.
records.quote: The reorder buffer stores the individual micro-ops in the original program order and retires as many as three per clock in the retirement register file (RRF). This file examines each completed micro-op for the presence of faults or branch mispredictions, and halts further retirement upon detecting such a discontinuity.

records.current_value: Timestamps reimpose program order; retire writes result to RRF and notifies RAT; up to 3 retire/clock; flush on mispredict
records.fact: Retirement mechanics: retirement hardware uses uop timestamps to reimpose program order; when a uop retires the ROB writes its result into the appropriate RRF entry and notifies the RAT; up to 3 uops retire per clock; on a mispredict the machine flushes all or part of its state
records.notes: Level-3 record: the timestamp mechanism and the RRF/RAT commit path; the flush-on-mispredict sentence is 'This retirement process must observe not only the original program order, it must correctly handle interrupts and faults, and flush all or part of its state on detection of a mispredicted branch.'
records.quote: Retirement hardware in the ROB uses uop timestamps to reimpose the original program order on the uops as their results are committed to permanent architectural machine state in the Retirement Register File (RRF). When a uop is retired, the ROB writes that uop's result into the appropriate RRF entry and notifies the RAT of that retirement so that subsequent register renaming can be activated. Up to 3 uops can be retired per clock cycle.

records.current_value: XP = switch/router module, fundamental mesh building block; 4/3/2 mesh ports and 2/3/4 device ports by position; max 144 XPs, 12x12 grid
records.fact: The CMN-700 Crosspoint (XP) is a switch/router logic module and the fundamental building block of the mesh transport; interior XPs have 4 mesh + 2 device ports, edge XPs 3 + 3, corner XPs 2 + 4; the mesh tops out at 144 XPs in a 12 x 12 grid addressed by (X,Y) coordinates
records.notes: Level-3 record: underpins the mesh-crosspoint crossbar primitive; the per-position port counts are the §3.1.1.1 table (4 mesh/2 device interior, 3/3 edge, 2/4 corner).
records.quote: The Crosspoint (XP) is a switch or router logic module. It is the fundamental component building block of the CMN-700 transport mechanism. The maximum size for the CMN-700 mesh is 144 XPs arranged in a 12 × 12 grid. Each XP in the grid is referenced using an (X,Y) coordinate system.

records.fact: CMN-700 uses credited end-to-end protocol-layer flow control with a retry-once mechanism for flexible bandwidth and resource allocation

source.title: Arm Neoverse CMN-700 Coherent Mesh Network Technical Reference Manual (102308_0307_08_en, Issue 08)

records.current_value: One link-layer credit per flit, returned one at a time; continuous transmission without credit stalls required for full bandwidth
records.fact: Link-layer credit flow control: one credit per flit, credits returned one at a time as flits are processed; a transmitter must be able to send continuously without stalling on credits to reach full link bandwidth
records.notes: Level-3 record: the credit-counter mechanism; the no-stall condition is the same section's 'A transmitting device must be able to send flits continuously in a pipelined fashion without stalling because of insufficient link layer credits from the receiving device.'
records.quote: A flow-control mechanism by which the transmitting device uses link layer credits to send CHI flits – one credit per flit. In turn, the receiving device sends these credits back to the transmitting device, one at a time, when it is done processing each flit to allow for subsequent flit transfers.

records.current_value: HN-F = SLC slice + combined PoS/PoC + SF; SLC exclusive for data, pseudo-inclusive for code
records.fact: Each HN-F holds a System Level Cache slice, a combined Point-of-Serialization/Point-of-Coherency and a Snoop Filter; the SLC allocation policy is exclusive for data lines and pseudo-inclusive for code lines
records.notes: Level-3 record: underpins the HN-F SLC SRAM-bank and PoS/PoC FSM primitives.
records.quote: The System Level Cache (SLC) is a last-level cache. The SLC allocation policy is exclusive for data lines, except where sharing patterns are detected and pseudo-inclusive for code lines, as indicated by the RN-Fs. The combined Point-of-Serialization/Point-of-Coherency (PoS/PoC) is responsible for the ordering of all memory requests sent to the HN-F.

source.title: Arm Neoverse CMN-700 Coherent Mesh Network Technical Reference Manual (102308_0307_08_en, Issue 08)

records.current_value: SF tracks lines present in RN-Fs; directed snoops preferred over broadcasts
records.fact: The Snoop Filter tracks cachelines present in the RN-Fs and favours directed snoops over snoop broadcasts, substantially reducing snoop response traffic
records.notes: Level-3 record: underpins the snoop-filter CAM primitive.
records.quote: The Snoop Filter (SF) tracks cachelines that are present in the RN-Fs. It reduces snoop traffic in the system by favoring directed snoops over snoop broadcasts when possible. This approach substantially reduces the snoop response traffic that might otherwise be required.

source.title: Arm Neoverse CMN-700 Coherent Mesh Network Technical Reference Manual (102308_0307_08_en, Issue 08)

records.current_value: Optimal total SF size = 2x total exclusive RN-F cache size
records.fact: The optimal total Snoop Filter size is twice the total exclusive cache size for all RN-Fs
records.notes: Level-3 record: the SF sizing rule; e.g. a 32MB RN-F total cache size implies a 64MB recommended SF size (same section).
records.quote: The optimal total SF size is twice the total exclusive cache size for all RN-Fs.

records.current_value: SLC per HN-F 0K-4M (12/16 ways); SF tag RAM per HN-F 512K-16M; POCQ 16-128 entries (default 32)
records.fact: Per-HN-F system cache is 0K-4M in 12 or 16 ways; per-HN-F snoop-filter tag RAM is 512K-16M; the Point-of-Coherency Queue tracker holds 16-128 entries (default 32)
records.notes: Level-3 record: the HN-F sizing parameters behind the SLC-bank, SF-CAM and PoS/PoC primitives; the SLC 0K-4M range and 12/16 ways, and the POCQ 16-128 (default 32) depths, are the same table's parameter values.
records.quote: SF_SIZE = (32K * (2^SF_SIZE_PARAM) * SF_NUM_WAYS). SF_NUM_WAYS = 16: 512K, 1M, 2M, 4M, 8M. SF_NUM_WAYS = 32: 1M, 2M, 4M, 8M, 16M.

records.current_value: Credited slices: MCS 0-4 per XP-XP link; AMCS performs clock-domain crossing
records.fact: Credited Slices enable synchronous but higher-latency communication anywhere in the system; mesh credited slices run 0-4 per XP-XP link and asynchronous mesh credited slices perform clock-domain crossing
records.notes: Level-3 record: underpins the credited-slice pipeline-register primitive; the AMCS clock-domain-crossing role is §3.1.1.14.2 ('Asynchronous Mesh Credited Slices (AMCSs) perform clock domain crossing between two asynchronous mesh clock domains.') and the 0-4 counts are the mesh-sizing table.
records.quote: Credited Slices enable synchronous but higher latency communication at any point in the system. You can configure one or more Mesh Credited Slices (MCSs) between CMN-700 XPs. MCSs are optional register slices that can help timing closure in a CMN-700 system.

records.current_value: L2 8 MiB/CMG, 16-way, 256-byte lines, PIPT, MESI, 37-47 cycle hit latency, 2 banks interleaved at bit[8], hashed 11-bit index

records.current_value: RSA/RSE/RSBR are out-of-order schedulers; CSE reorders to program order; WB holds post-commit stores
records.fact: Reservation stations are schedulers that temporarily store operation-flows and issue them out of order (RSA for EAGA/EAGB, RSE for EXA/EXB/FLA/FLB/PR, RSBR for branches); the CSE reorders out-of-order execution into program order; the write buffer temporarily stores post-commit store data until written to the L1D cache
records.notes: CSE definition: 'This resource is used to reorder instructions executed out of order into program order.' WB definition: 'This resource is used to temporarily store post-commit store data until it is written to the L1D cache.'
records.quote: This RS is a scheduler for temporarily storing operation-flows to be executed in the EAGA/EAGB pipeline and issuing them out of order.

records.current_value: CMG = 13 cores + L2 + memory controller; 4 CMGs ccNUMA with on-chip directory; X-bar joins cores to L2

records.notes: URL is a SlideShare mirror of Fujitsu's Hot Chips 30 deck, read live this run. Companion quotes from the same slide: 'Four CMGs keep cache coherency by ccNUMA with on-chip directory.' and 'X-bar connection in a CMG maximizes high efficiency for throughput of the L2 cache.'

records.current_value: 4 slices + 1 MME per SMT4 half; each slice: VS RF + VU
records.fact: POWER10 backend per SMT4 half: four execution slices ES[0:3] plus one attached Matrix Math Engine; each slice contains a vector-scalar register file (VS RF) and a vector execution unit (VU)
records.notes: Companion sentence: 'An execution slice contains a register file (VS RF) for the 128-bit wide vector-scalar registers and an execution unit (VU) for performing operations on those registers.'
records.quote: The backend consists of four (4) execution slices (ES[0:3]) and an attached matrix math engine (MME).

source.locator: Section III, Implementation in the POWER10 Processor
source.title: A matrix math facility for Power ISA(TM) processors

records.current_value: 1 issue/cycle/slice; MMA issue only from slices 2 and 3
records.fact: Each execution slice issues one instruction per cycle; slices 2 and 3 can issue either a vector instruction or an MMA instruction, slices 0 and 1 can only issue vector instructions
records.notes: Companion sentence: 'Slices 2 and 3 can issue either a vector instruction or an MMA instruction. Slices 0 and 1 can only issue vector instructions.'
records.quote: On a given cycle, each slice can issue one instruction for execution.

source.locator: Section III, Implementation in the POWER10 Processor
source.title: A matrix math facility for Power ISA(TM) processors

records.current_value: 2 pipelines (MU2, MU3) sharing one ACC RF; 2 rank-k updates/cycle per MME
records.fact: MME logically consists of two execution pipelines (MU2 and MU3, for instructions issued from slices 2 and 3) sharing a common accumulator register file (ACC RF); supports two rank-k update instructions per cycle
records.notes: Companion sentence: 'This organization supports the execution of two rank-k update instructions per cycle.'
records.quote: The matrix math engine logically consists of two (2) execution pipelines (MU2 and MU3 for instructions issued from slices 2 and 3, respectively) sharing a common accumulator register file (ACC RF).

source.locator: Section III, Implementation in the POWER10 Processor
source.title: A matrix math facility for Power ISA(TM) processors

records.current_value: 4x2 PU grid per MME; 2 halves per PU; 64-bit ACC RF slice per half, 2 read + 1 write ports
records.fact: MME physical implementation is a 4x2 grid of processing units (PU); each PU has two identical halves, one per issuing slice; each half includes a 64-bit slice of the accumulator register file with two read and one write ports
records.notes: Companion sentences: 'Each processing unit has two identical halves, one for each of the issuing slices (2 and 3). Each half includes a 64-bit slice of the accumulator register file (ACC2 and ACC3) with two read and one write ports.' Figure 3 caption: 'Each matrix unit consists of a 4 × 2 grid of basic tiles. Each tile has a 64-bit slice of the accumulator register file (each accumulator is 512 bits wide) and the corresponding multiply-add functional units to operate on that data slice.'
records.quote: The physical implementation of the MME is shown in Figure 3 and consists of a 4 × 2 grid of processing units (PU).

source.locator: Section III, Implementation in the POWER10 Processor
source.title: A matrix math facility for Power ISA(TM) processors

records.current_value: Per PU half: 1 DP or 2 SP FMA; 4/8/16 MACs of 16/8/4-bit data
records.fact: Each PU-half ALU performs one double-precision or two single-precision floating-point multiply-adds, or 4, 8, or 16 multiply-adds of 16-, 8-, or 4-bit data; each ALU result is written to the corresponding accumulator register file while its input can come from either half
records.notes: Companion sentences: 'It can also perform 4, 8, or 16 multiply-adds of 16-, 8-, or 4-bit data, respectively. The result of each ALU is always written to the corresponding accumulator register file but the input can come from either one. (Hence the requirement for two read ports.)' Arithmetic: 8 PUs x 2 halves x 1 DP FMA = 16 DP FMAs = 32 FLOPs/cycle per MME; x2 MMEs per SMT8 core = 64 FP64 FLOPs/cycle, matching Thompto's verified figure. INT4: 8 x 2 x 16 = 256 MACs = 512 ops/cycle per MME; x2 = 1,024 ops/cycle per core.
records.quote: The arithmetic and logic unit in each half (ALU2 and ALU3) can perform one double-precision or two single-precision floating-point multiply-add(s).

source.locator: Section III, Implementation in the POWER10 Processor
source.title: A matrix math facility for Power ISA(TM) processors

records.current_value: VSR->ACC 2 cycles; ACC->VSR 4 cycles; up to 2 simultaneous transfers
records.fact: Fetch buses bring X and Y operands from the vector-scalar register files to the MME; result buses transfer accumulator data back to the VSRs; 2 cycles to transfer four VSRs to an accumulator, 4 cycles to transfer one accumulator to four VSRs, up to two transfers simultaneously
records.notes: Companion sentences: 'The fetch buses from the vector-scalar register files bring X and Y operands for the outer product instructions and transfer data from the vector-scalar registers to the accumulators.' and 'Up to two transfers can be performed simultaneously.' Arithmetic: 512 bits in 2 cycles = 256 bits/cycle in; 512 bits in 4 cycles = 128 bits/cycle out.
records.quote: It takes two (2) cycles to transfer four (4) vector-scalar registers to an accumulator and four (4) cycles to transfer one accumulator to 4 vector-scalar registers.

source.locator: Section III, Implementation in the POWER10 Processor
source.title: A matrix math facility for Power ISA(TM) processors

records.current_value: Accumulator data stays local to the MME during computation; no result-bus output
records.fact: During the computation phase of a math kernel the accumulator data stays local to the Matrix Math Engine and no output is placed on the result buses, making execution more power efficient
records.notes: Companion sentence: 'Only the X and Y inputs have to be brought from the register files. Furthermore, no output is placed on the results buses. This leads to a more power efficient execution of those kernels.'
records.quote: During the computation phase of a math kernel, the accumulator data stays local to the matrix math engine.

records.current_value: MME power-gatable; zero MME draw when running VSX code
records.fact: The MME unit can be power gated, eliminating MME power draw when running VSX code
records.notes: From the paper's power results: the POWER10 core running MMA code delivers 2.5x the performance of the same core running VSX code while drawing only 8% more power; power-gating the MME widens that difference to 12%.

records.current_value: 16-way set-associative; 16 channels per HBM stack; 64-byte channel width; 2 MB data arrays per channel, banked for simultaneous reads and writes
records.fact: Infinity Cache is 16-way set-associative, built around channels; each HBM stack has 16 parallel channels, each channel 64 bytes wide, connected to 2 MB of banked data arrays
records.notes: Level-3 record: the channel geometry is the published basis for the Level-3 decomposition's SRAM-bank, CAM/tag-array, comparator and mux/demux primitives (64-byte channel width, 2 MB per channel).
records.quote: Just like the L2 cache, the AMD Infinity Cache is 16-way set-associative, and it is built around the concept of channels. Each stack of HBM memory is associated with 16 parallel channels. A channel is 64-bytes wide and connects to 2 MB of data arrays that are banked to sustain simultaneous reads and writes.

source.title: Introducing AMD CDNA 3 Architecture

records.current_value: 128 channels, 256 MB (128 x 2 MB); 32 channels / 64 MB per IOD and 32 MB per HBM stack by arithmetic
records.fact: Eight HBM stacks across four IODs, 128 Infinity Cache channels, 256 MB of cache data
records.notes: Level-3 record. Corroborated by the Hot Chips 2024 deck block diagram, which draws the Infinity Cache as 128 two-megabyte blocks, and by the data sheet's 256 MB figure.
records.quote: In total, there are eight stacks of HBM across the four IODs, for 128 channels or 256MB of data.

source.title: Introducing AMD CDNA 3 Architecture

records.current_value: 17.2 TB/s per the CDNA 3 white paper; 14.7 TB/s per the Hot Chips 2024 deck
records.fact: Infinity Cache peak bandwidth: 17.2 TB/s (CDNA 3 white paper) vs 14.7 TB/s (Hot Chips 2024 deck)
records.notes: Disputed between two AMD sources: the Hot Chips 2024 deck (Smith & Alla, 'MI300X Cache and Memory Hierarchy' slide) states '256 MB at 14.7 TB/s peak BW'. The 17.2 TB/s figure is consistent with the published geometry at peak clock: 128 channels x 64 bytes x 2.1 GHz = 17.2 TB/s, and with the 1 KB-per-XCD interface x 8 XCDs at 2.1 GHz. The 14.7 TB/s figure corresponds to the same 8,192 bytes/cycle at ~1.8 GHz, i.e. a lower sustained clock. The Level-3 section quotes 17.2 TB/s as the peak and flags the deck's 14.7 TB/s. Independent analysis (Chips and Cheese, Dec 2023) independently derives 17.2 TB/s at 2.1 GHz.
records.quote: The peak bandwidth from the Infinity Cache is an astounding 17.2 TB/s, which is nearly as much as the total from the previous generation L2 caches and a welcome addition to the overall memory hierarchy.

source.title: Introducing AMD CDNA 3 Architecture

records.current_value: Memory-side cache; no dirty data; no coherency participation; no snoop traffic; can cache uncacheable I/O buffers
records.fact: Infinity Cache is a shared memory-side cache: caches memory contents, cannot hold dirty data evicted from a lower-level cache, does not participate in coherency and absorbs no snoop traffic, and can hold nominally uncacheable memory such as I/O buffers
records.notes: Level-3 record: the memory-side design is the published basis for the FSM/controller primitive (fills come only from HBM; no dirty-writeback handling) and for the snoop-filter register-file primitive. The same passage continues: 'First, the AMD Infinity Cache doesn't participate in coherency and does not have to absorb or handle any snoop traffic, which significantly improves efficiency and reduces the latency of snooping from lower level caches. Second, it can actually hold nominally uncacheable memory such as buffers for I/O.'
records.quote: The AMD Infinity Cache was carefully designed as a shared memory-side cache, meaning that it caches the contents of memory and cannot hold dirty data evicted from a lower level cache.

source.title: Introducing AMD CDNA 3 Architecture

records.current_value: Snoop filter covering the multiple XCD L2 caches
records.fact: Infinity Cache includes a snoop filter covering the multiple XCD L2 caches, resolving most coherent requests from other XCDs without disturbing the L2s
records.notes: Level-3 record: the snoop filter is the published basis for the register-file primitive. The quote is reproduced exactly as printed, including the source's doubled 'other other'; the sentence continues past a page break in the PDF ('without disturbing ...'), so the quote is cut at the page break rather than completed from inference.
records.quote: The Infinity Cache includes a snoop filter covering the multiple XCD L2 caches so that the vast majority of coherent requests from other other XCDs will be resolved at the Infinity Cache

source.title: Introducing AMD CDNA 3 Architecture

records.current_value: 4 MB, 16-way, 16 x 256 KB channels; 128-byte read line; 4 requests/cycle; 2 KB/clock per XCD; 1 fill/clock per channel
records.fact: L2 is 4 MB, 16-way set-associative, 16 channels of 256 KB; reads a 128-byte line per channel, sustains four requests from different CUs per cycle for 2 KB/clock per XCD, with one fill request from the Infinity Fabric per clock per channel
records.notes: Level-3 record: the L2 geometry bounds the Infinity Cache from above and is the published basis for the FIFO/queue and credit-counter primitives (one fill per clock per channel). The same passage continues: 'On the read side each channel can read out a 128-byte cache line and the L2 cache can sustain four requests from different CUs per cycle for a combined throughput of 2KBytes/clock for each XCD. The 16 channels only support a half-line 64-byte write each with one fill request from the Infinity Fabric per clock.' The 128-byte line belongs to the L2 and is NOT claimed for the Infinity Cache.
records.quote: The L2 is a 4MB and 16-way set associative cache that is massively parallel with 16 channels that are each 256KB.

source.title: Introducing AMD CDNA 3 Architecture

records.current_value: 16 channels x 64 bytes = 1,024 bytes per XCD at the IOD interface; ~2.15 TB/s per XCD at 2.1 GHz by arithmetic
records.fact: Each L2 connects to its IOD across sixteen 64-byte channels, 1 KB per XCD at the IOD interface
records.notes: Level-3 record: the 1 KB-per-XCD interface is the published basis for the mux/demux and synchronizer primitives. The ~2.15 TB/s per-XCD figure is arithmetic (1,024 bytes x 2.1 GHz peak engine clock), and 8 XCDs give ~17.2 TB/s aggregate, matching the Infinity Cache peak bandwidth; the Hot Chips 2024 deck labels the XCD/IOD interface at 2.1 TB/s.
records.quote: Each L2 is connected to the IOD across the set of sixteen channels and each channel is 64-bytes wide, for a total of 1K-bytes per XCD at the IOD interface.

source.title: Introducing AMD CDNA 3 Architecture

records.current_value: IODs on TSMC 6nm, stacked beneath a pair of XCDs; contain Infinity Cache + HBM3 interface; connected by Infinity Fabric
records.fact: IODs are TSMC 6 nm, vertically stacked beneath a pair of XCDs, and contain the Infinity Cache and the HBM3 interface
records.notes: Level-3 record: the 6 nm IOD / 5 nm XCD split is the published basis for the synchronizer primitive (die-boundary, cross-process-node crossing). The data sheet confirms 'I/O Dies (IODs) 6nm FinFET' against 5nm FinFET compute.
records.quote: The IODs are manufactured on TSMC's 6nm process and vertically stacked beneath a pair of XCDs. They contain a brand new AMD Infinity Cache and the HBM3 interface to the on-package memory and are connected to the rest of the system by the AMD Infinity Fabric network.

source.title: Introducing AMD CDNA 3 Architecture

records.current_value: 5.2 Gbps bus; 24 GB per stack; 192 GB total; 5.3 TB/s
records.fact: HBM3 memory controllers drive a 5.2 Gbps bus; each MI300X stack holds 24 GB; 192 GB total at 5.3 TB/s peak theoretical bandwidth
records.notes: Level-3 record: the HBM geometry is the published basis for the FSM/controller (HBM controller) and counter primitives. The 192 GB / 5.3 TB/s totals are also stated in the MI300X data sheet ('Memory capacity Up to 192 GB HBM3', 'Memory bandwidth 5.3 TB/s max. peak theoretical').

records.current_value: 144K pixels = 768 pixels wide and 192 pixels tall; maximum tile column width 512 pixels; 128-pixel horizontal search window on each side; LRU eviction
records.fact: Reference store is a 144K-pixel SRAM array (768 wide x 192 tall) holding the motion-search window, sized around a 512-pixel tile column with 128-pixel horizontal search windows, with LRU eviction
records.notes: Second supporting sentence from the same section: 'The reference store supports LRU eviction.' Footnote 4: '144K pixels = 768 pixels wide and 192 pixels tall.' 768 x 192 = 147,456 = 144K exactly. The footnote's tile-column arithmetic renders as '8x84-pixel macroblocks' in PDF text extraction; 512 / 8 = 64, so this is read as eight 64-pixel macroblocks.
records.quote: Consequently, a key element of our design is an SRAM array reference store that holds the motion search window.

source.title: Warehouse-Scale Video Acceleration: Co-Design and Deployment in the Wild

records.current_value: 394K pixels (2048 x 128) raster store for H.264; up to 2048-pixel-wide video
records.fact: For H.264 the reference store is reconfigured as a raster store of 64x16-pixel blocks and grown to 394K pixels (2048 x 128), supporting video up to 2048 pixels wide
records.notes: Arithmetic flag, recorded not silently corrected: 2048 x 128 = 262,144 luma pixels (256K); the paper's 394K figure reconciles if it counts luma + 4:2:0 chroma samples (262,144 x 1.5 = 393,216, i.e. ~394K in decimal thousands). Recorded as published.
records.quote: For H.264, which lacks tile columns, the reference store is configured as a raster store of 64x16 pixel blocks. By increasing the reference store to 394K pixels (2048 x 128), the core can provide efficient encoding for up to 2048 pixel wide videos.

source.title: Warehouse-Scale Video Acceleration: Co-Design and Deployment in the Wild

records.current_value: 16x16 macroblock for H.264; 64x64 superblock for VP9
records.fact: Pipeline unit of work is a 16x16 macroblock (H.264) or a 64x64 superblock (VP9)
records.quote: The basic element of the pipelined computation is either a 16x16 macroblock (H.264) or a 64x64 superblock (VP9) – the largest square group of pixels that a codec operates on at a time.

source.title: Warehouse-Scale Video Acceleration: Co-Design and Deployment in the Wild

records.current_value: FIFO-decoupled stages with full backpressure
records.fact: Pipeline stages are decoupled with FIFOs and full FIFO backpressure stalls upstream stages when needed
records.notes: Context: stage costs vary per macroblock because of the wide variety of blocks and modes, so the stages run at different rates.
records.quote: To address this, the pipeline stages are decoupled with FIFOs, and full FIFO backpressure is used to stall upstream stages when needed.

source.title: Warehouse-Scale Video Acceleration: Co-Design and Deployment in the Wild

records.current_value: Exhaustive multi-resolution motion search to 1/8-pixel
records.fact: Motion search is exhaustive and multi-resolution, down to 1/8-pixel resolution, using the local search memory
records.quote: Additionally, the local search memory allows for an exhaustive, multi-resolution motion search (down to 1/8th pixel resolution), achieving higher throughput and better results than are typically obtained in a software motion estimation implementation.

source.title: Warehouse-Scale Video Acceleration: Co-Design and Deployment in the Wild

records.current_value: Bounded recursive partition search; programmable RDO round count
records.fact: Partitioning uses a bounded recursive search balancing coding overhead against error reduction; the number of RDO rounds is programmable
records.notes: Second supporting sentence: 'Per-codec logic selects from a number of transform/prediction mode candidates using approximate encoding/decoding to optimize bit rate and quality, and the number of rounds can be programmed.'
records.quote: A bounded recursive search algorithm is used for partitioning, balancing the coding overhead of smaller partitions against a reduction in net error.

source.title: Warehouse-Scale Video Acceleration: Co-Design and Deployment in the Wild

records.current_value: Temporal filter aligns 16x16 blocks from 3 frames; synthetic alternate reference frames; iterative application possible
records.fact: Temporal filtering aligns 16x16-pixel blocks from 3 frames and emits filtered blocks, creating synthetic alternate reference frames; it can be applied iteratively to filter more than 3 frames
records.notes: Second supporting sentence: 'The temporal filter can be iteratively applied to filter more than 3 frames, providing an additional quality/speed trade-off.'
records.quote: It uses motion estimation to align 16x16 pixel blocks from 3 frames and emits new filtered blocks with low temporal noise.

source.title: Warehouse-Scale Video Acceleration: Co-Design and Deployment in the Wild

records.current_value: Loop filter uses local SRAM line buffers for adjacent and top block pixels
records.fact: Loop filtering reads pixels from adjacent and top blocks held in local SRAM line buffers
records.notes: 'The former' is loop filtering, in the sentence: 'The final stage of the pipeline takes the decoded output of the encode block and applies loop filtering and lossless frame buffer compression.'
records.quote: The former requires access to pixels from adjacent and top blocks, which are stored in local SRAM line buffers.

source.title: Warehouse-Scale Video Acceleration: Co-Design and Deployment in the Wild

records.current_value: Lossless proprietary per-macroblock frame-buffer compression; ~50% reference read-bandwidth reduction
records.fact: Frame-buffer compression is lossless and proprietary, cutting reference-frame memory read bandwidth by approximately 50%
records.notes: The paper calls the algorithm proprietary ('losslessly compresses each macroblock with a proprietary algorithm'); no compression method is published.
records.quote: The frame buffer compression reduces reference frame memory read bandwidth by approximately 50%.

source.title: Warehouse-Scale Video Acceleration: Co-Design and Deployment in the Wild

records.current_value: 11.9 MiB per 2160p raw frame; 3.5 GiB/s average, ~3 GiB/s worst case, 2 GiB/s typical per encoder core
records.fact: Per-core DRAM bandwidth at 2160p: 11.9 MiB raw frame, 3.5 GiB/s average (one input frame and three references read, one reference written), ~3 GiB/s worst case and 2 GiB/s typical with reference compression
records.notes: Second supporting sentence: 'While the access pattern causes some data to be read multiple times, the lossless reference compression reduces the worst-case bandwidth to ~3 GiB/s and typical bandwidth to 2 GiB/s.'
records.quote: At 2160p, each raw frame is 11.9 MiB, giving an average DRAM bandwidth of 3.5 GiB/s (reading one input frame and three references and writing one reference).

source.title: Warehouse-Scale Video Acceleration: Co-Design and Deployment in the Wild

records.current_value: Four 32b LPDDR4-3200 channels, ~36 GiB/s raw; VCU needs ~27-37 GiB/s; decoder 2.2 GiB/s
records.fact: VCU DRAM: four 32b LPDDR4-3200 channels, ~36 GiB/s raw bandwidth, against a ~27-37 GiB/s need; the decoder consistently uses 2.2 GiB/s
records.quote: The decoder consistently uses 2.2 GiB/s, so the VCU needs ~27-37 GiB/s of DRAM bandwidth, which we provide with four 32b LPDDR4-3200 channels (~36 GiB/s of raw bandwidth).

source.title: Warehouse-Scale Video Acceleration: Co-Design and Deployment in the Wild

records.current_value: 8 GiB usable; six x32 DRAM chips; side-band SECDED ECC
records.fact: 8 GiB usable VCU DRAM on six x32 DRAM chips, with the extra capacity used for side-band SECDED ECC
records.notes: Second supporting sentence: 'Other system resources to be balanced were VCU DRAM capacity (the 8 GiB usable capacity gave modest headroom for all workloads)'.
records.quote: These are attached to six x32 DRAM chips, with the additional capacity used for side-band SECDED ECC [26].

source.title: Warehouse-Scale Video Acceleration: Co-Design and Deployment in the Wild

records.current_value: Dozens of outstanding memory operations per core; memory barrier at the end of each tile column
records.fact: Each encoder core can have dozens of outstanding memory operations in flight; the out-of-order memory subsystem's one hazard (cross-tile-boundary macroblocks for the in-loop deblocking filter) is handled by a memory barrier at the end of each tile column
records.notes: Second supporting sentence: 'The primary hazard is the use of cross-tile boundary macroblocks for the in-loop deblocking filter, which is avoided by a memory barrier at the end of each tile column.' The exact maximum outstanding count is not published — only 'dozens'.
records.quote: Consequently, each core in our design can have dozens of outstanding memory operations in flight.

source.title: Warehouse-Scale Video Acceleration: Co-Design and Deployment in the Wild

records.current_value: Control/status registers per operation; stateless — all inputs and outputs in VCU DRAM
records.fact: The encoder IP block is programmed via control/status registers per operation, and all inputs (frame, reference frames, QP look-up tables, probability tables, temporal motion vectors) and outputs (encoded frame, updated reference frame, temporal motion vectors, updated probability tables) live in VCU DRAM — a stateless core
records.notes: Second supporting sentence: 'All inputs – the frame to be encoded, all reference frames, other auxiliary inputs (quantization parameter look-up tables, probability tables, temporal motion vectors) – are stored in VCU DRAM, as are all the outputs – the encoded frame, the updated reference frame, temporal motion vectors and updated probability tables.'
records.quote: The encoder IP block is programmed via a set of control/status registers for each operation.

source.title: Warehouse-Scale Video Acceleration: Co-Design and Deployment in the Wild

records.current_value: Bool coder: one boolean per step against an estimated probability; 16-bit integers and one unsigned 16-bit multiply
records.fact: VP9's bool coder decodes one boolean value at a time given an estimated probability, working with a small set of unsigned 16-bit integers and an unsigned 16-bit multiplication operation
records.notes: Second supporting sentence: 'The boolean decoder works using a small set of unsigned 16-bit integers and an unsigned 16-bit multiplication operation.' The specification defines the decoder side; Argos's encoder implements the same arithmetic in the encode direction. The wiki's Building blocks already state the coder is a boolean arithmetic coder; this record supplies the primary-source basis.
records.quote: At the lowest level VP9 contains a boolean decoder which decodes one boolean value (0 or 1) at a time given an input containing the estimated probability of the value.

source.title: VP9 Bitstream & Decoding Process Specification

records.current_value: ~140 MiB reference frames at 2160p VP9 10-bit; ~420 MiB MOT footprint; ~180-220 MiB for 15 two-pass frames; ~700 MiB per MOT / 500 MiB per SOT largest 2160p footprint; +~5% footprint from reference compression
records.fact: Reference compression adds ~5% to the DRAM footprint; a 2160p VP9 10-bit encode needs ~140 MiB for reference frames (8 plus 1 output); a multi-output transcode footprint is ~420 MiB, 15 frames for lagged/offline two-pass need ~180-220 MiB, and the largest expected 2160p footprint is roughly 700 MiB per MOT and 500 MiB per SOT
records.notes: Second supporting sentence: 'The decode and encode footprint for MOT comes to ~420 MiB. Keeping up to 15 frames for lagged and offline two-pass encoding modes requires ~180-220 MiB. Padding requirements and ephemeral buffers brings the expected largest, 2160p total footprint to roughly 700 MiB per MOT and 500 MiB per SOT.' And: 'The encoder core's reference compression significantly reduces the DRAM bandwidth but slightly increases (+~5%) the DRAM footprint.'
records.quote: The maximum expected 2160p resolution in VP9 with 10-bit color depth gives ~140 MiB for reference frames (8 plus 1 output).

source.title: Warehouse-Scale Video Acceleration: Co-Design and Deployment in the Wild

records.current_value: 3 decoder cores and 10 encoder cores per VCU
records.fact: Each VCU carries 3 decoder cores beside its 10 encoder cores (3,000 millidecode cores and 10,000 milliencode cores per VCU)
records.notes: Corroborated by Figure 3b, the VCU block diagram, which shows three decoder cores and ten encoder cores. The encoder-core count itself was already recorded in the 2026-11-22 Level-2 pass; the decoder-core count is new.
records.quote: Figure 6 illustrates our design with VCU workers showing just the decoder (D) and encoder (E) core dimensions. To avoid fractions, the core dimensions use millicores so each VCU has 3,000 millidecode cores and 10,000 milliencode cores available.

records.current_value: Gate-level detail not published; decomposition is textbook-standard construction, labelled as such
records.fact: Level-4 boundary: gate-level structure not published for the Argos encoder core - reference-store bank/port counts and turnaround; LRU eviction circuit; motion-score circuit and candidates scored in parallel; reference-frame mux radix and compound-prediction datapath; partition-FSM state count and recursion bound; RDO candidate count and cost widths; transform-array geometry and interpolation-filter structure; loop-filter line-buffer sizes; frame-buffer-compression algorithm and datapath; bool-coder throughput, renormalisation-shifter form and bit-packing width; probability-table sizes and adaptation datapath; FIFO depths and widths; outstanding-operation maximum and counter widths; control-register map; pipeline-latch widths and stage latencies; NoC width, arbitration and credit-counter depths
records.notes: Level-4 honesty record: Ranganathan et al., ASPLOS 2021 publishes the pipeline stages, the reference-store geometry (144K pixels, 768 x 192, LRU eviction; the H.264 raster store at '394K pixels (2048 x 128)'), the 16x16 macroblock / 64x64 superblock unit of work, the exhaustive multi-resolution motion search down to 1/8-pixel against three reference frames, the temporal filter's 16x16 blocks from 3 frames, the ~50% reference-read-bandwidth saving from frame-buffer compression, the per-core DRAM budget and the VCU memory system, but no gate/transistor implementation; the VP9 specification adds the bool coder's construction (one boolean at a time; 16-bit integers and one 16-bit multiply). Arithmetic in the section is from those published geometries at a stated 8-bit-per-sample assumption (768 x 192 = 147,456 pixels x 8 bits = 1,179,648 bits = 7,077,888 6T cell transistors for the VP9 store; 2048 x 128 = 262,144 pixels x 8 bits = 2,097,152 bits = 12,582,912 cell transistors for the H.264 geometry; 8-bit row decode for 192 rows, 7-bit for 128; 256 partial products in a 16x16 multiply). One published figure is flagged, not used: the paper's '394K pixels (2048 x 128)' does not multiply out (2048 x 128 = 262,144), so no transistor total is claimed from '394K' itself.

records.notes: Bennetts, Boundary Scan Tutorial v2.1, Fig. 34 text and Fig. 33 (controller drawn as a Moore machine). The 4-bit state-register width in the section is arithmetic from the 16 states (2^4 = 16), labelled as such.
records.quote: A state transition occurs on the positive edge of TCK and the controller output values change on the negative edge of TCK.

records.fact: Gate-level structure not published: no NVIDIA source discloses the Ada SM's, the SER reorder stage's or the OFA's per-primitive gate/transistor implementation (register-file cell style and port count; mux radix and operand-collection width; scheduler issue-queue and SER queue depths; warp-scheduler and reorder-controller state counts and regrouping policy; SER grouping-key width; Tensor Core dimensions, partial-product structure and FP8 encoding; adder-tree depth and carry structure; L0 size and L1 bank count, line size and associativity; SM crossbar radix, port counts and arbitration policy; stage counts and latch widths; L1 tag-array associativity and geometry; OFA buffer sizes, algorithm, block size, search range and stage count). All gate-level detail in the Level-4 decomposition is textbook-standard construction, labelled as such.
records.notes: Level-4 boundary honesty record, following the MBIST/Argos/JTAG pattern. Arithmetic figures in the section (256 KB register file per SM = 2,097,152 bits = 12,582,912 6T cell transistors per SM; 36 MB die register file = 1,811,939,328; 128 KB L1 per SM = 1,048,576 bits = 6,291,456; 18 MB die L1 = 905,969,664; 96 MB L2 context = 4,831,838,208) are derived from the published geometries and check exactly against the whitepaper's own die totals (144 SMs, 36 MB register file, 18 MB L1, 96 MB L2, 76.3 billion transistors). The SER synchronizer primitive decomposes to zero gates: reconvergence is logical, not a clock-domain crossing.

records.fact: VOPD instruction encodes two separate VALU operations executed in parallel, legal only in wave32 mode
records.notes: Same section: 'This instruction format is legal only for wave32. It must not be used by wave64's. It is skipped for wave64.'
records.quote: The VOPD instruction encoding allows a single shader instruction to encode two separate VALU operations that are executed in parallel.

source.title: "RDNA3" Instruction Set Architecture: Reference Guide

records.current_value: 4 VGPR banks; 3 read ports per bank cache; SRCX0/SRCY0 different banks, VSRCX1/VSRCY1 different banks
records.fact: VOPD register-bank rules: 4 VGPR banks, each bank cache has 3 read ports (SRC0/SRC1/SRC2); same-position sources must use different banks
records.notes: Same section: 'A cache can read all 3 of them at once, but it can't read two SRC0's at once (or SRC1/2).' and 'SRCX0 and SRCY0 must use different VGPR banks; VSRCX1 and VSRCY1 must use different banks.'
records.quote: There are 4 VGPR banks (indexed by SRC[1:0]), and each bank has a cache. Each cache has 3 read ports: one dedicated to SRC0, one dedicated to SRC1 and one for SRC2.

source.title: "RDNA3" Instruction Set Architecture: Reference Guide

records.current_value: One destination even, the other odd
records.fact: VOPD destination rule: the two destination VGPRs must be one even and one odd
records.notes: Field table: 'vdstX and vdstY: one must be even and the other is an odd VGPR.'
records.quote: Dest VGPRs: one must be even and the other odd.

source.title: "RDNA3" Instruction Set Architecture: Reference Guide

records.current_value: Simultaneous execution; no read-after-write race within a VOPD pair
records.fact: The two VOPD operations execute at the same time; a read of a VGPR the other writes gets the old value
records.quote: The two instructions in the VOPD are executed at the same time, so there are no races between them if one reads a VGPR and the other writes the same VGPR. The 'read' gets the old value.

source.title: "RDNA3" Instruction Set Architecture: Reference Guide

records.current_value: Wave64 = two issues per instruction (low half, high half); wave32 = at most one
records.fact: Wave64 waves issue each VALU/VMEM instruction twice (low half then high half); wave32 waves issue each instruction at most once
records.quote: Wave32 waves issue each instruction at most once. Wave64 waves typically issue each instruction twice: once for the low half (work-items 31-0) and then again for the high half (work-items 63-32).

records.current_value: No gate-level structure published; all Level-4 detail is textbook-standard construction
records.fact: Level-4 boundary: gate-level structure not published for Navi 31 - register-file cell style and write-port count; mux radix; issue-queue depths; scheduler state count and selection policy; VOPD comparator widths; SIMD32/WMMA multiplier geometry and tile sizes; adder-tree depth and carry structure; LDS crossbar radix; pipeline stage count; tag-array geometry and line sizes; LDS bank sense-amplifier form; credit-counter widths; barrier arrival-circuit form; barrel-shifter construction; and all MCD internals (cache controller, tag array, link arbiter, queue depths, bank counts, associativity, crossbar and clock-domain internals)
records.notes: Single honesty record scoping the Level-4 boundary for RDNA 3, following the MBIST/JTAG/Ada pattern. Arithmetic figures in the section (VGPR 384 KiB/CU = 3,145,728 bits = 18,874,368 6T cells/CU, 36 MB die-wide = 301,989,888 bits = 1,811,939,328 cells; LDS 128 KB/WGP = 1,048,576 bits = 6,291,456 cells, per bank 512x32 = 16,384 bits = 98,304 cells, 48 WGPs = 6 MB = 50,331,648 bits = 301,989,888 cells; L0 80 KB/CU = 655,360 bits = 3,932,160 cells, 96 CUs = 7.5 MB = 62,914,560 bits = 377,487,360 cells; L1 3 MB = 25,165,824 bits = 150,994,944 cells; L2 6 MB = 50,331,648 bits = 301,989,888 cells; Infinity Cache 96 MB = 805,306,368 bits = 4,831,838,208 cells, per MCD 16 MB = 134,217,728 bits = 805,306,368 cells; LDS 17-bit byte address, 16-bit work-group address, 6-bit bank index; barrel shifter 5 stages x 32 bits = 160 muxes) are derived transparently from the published geometries and the primer's bottom-layer cell forms, and are labelled standard construction in the text. Die-wide register-file totals rest on the Level-2 384 KiB VGPR value; the ROCm 6.3.2 vs 6.2.2 dispute (768 KiB / 16 KiB vs 384 KiB / 20 KiB) is recorded at Level-3. No GCD-specific transistor total is stated (Wikipedia 45.4bn vs Chips and Cheese 45.7bn). Secondary sources for the contract: AMD press release 3 Nov 2022; AMD ROCm GPU hardware specifications; PC Gamer Nov 2022 (Sam Naffziger); Chips and Cheese Jan 2023.

records.current_value: No gate-level structure published; all Level-4 detail is textbook-standard construction
records.fact: Level-4 boundary: gate-level structure not published for Ponte Vecchio - register-file cell style, size, entry count, bank count and port count; L1 instruction-cache size; mux radix and select encoding; XMX Booth encoding, compressor-tree structure and partial-product count; adder-tree depth and carry structure; barrel-shifter width, stage count and placement; L1/L3 tag widths, associativity and replacement policy; dispatch-controller state count and hazard handling; pipeline stage count and bypass network; crossbar radix and arbitration policy; LSU queue depth; credit counts and return latencies; MDFI radix, arbitration policy and queue depths; HBM controller queue depths and scheduling policy; FDI FIFO depths and widths; SerDes lane counts beyond the deck summary line and equalization; per-bank clock frequencies and PLL loop parameters; scan-chain lengths and test-mux forms
records.notes: Single honesty record scoping the Level-4 boundary for Ponte Vecchio, following the RDNA3/Ada/MBIST/JTAG pattern. Arithmetic figures in the section are derived transparently from the published geometries and the primer's bottom-layer cell forms, and are labelled standard construction in the text: L1 512 KB/core = 4,194,304 bits = 25,165,824 6T cells, 4 MB/tile = 33,554,432 bits = 201,326,592 cells, 64 MB/OAM = 536,870,912 bits = 3,221,225,472 cells; Rambo bank 3.75 MB = 31,457,280 bits = 188,743,680 cells, 32 banks = 1,006,632,960 bits = 6,039,797,760 cells; Memory Fabric 144 MB/base tile = 1,207,959,552 bits = 7,247,757,312 cells, 288 MB = 2,415,919,104 bits = 14,495,514,624 cells; whole second level 408 MB = 3,422,552,064 bits = 20,535,312,384 cells, about 20.5% of the published 100-billion-transistor package anchor (sanity check, not a netlist claim); 4096 B/cycle / 64 B per bank-op = 64 banks in parallel; 8 groups x 800 lanes = 6,400 FDI data lanes; 4x16 90G SERDES = 64 SerDes lanes; 512-bit XVE operand = 16 FP32 / 8 FP64 / 32 FP16 lanes, 4096-bit XMX operand = 512 INT8 / 256 BF16 lanes; 3-bit systolic step counter from the 8-deep array; 19-bit byte address for the 512 KB L1; 512-bit stage latch 10,240-14,336 transistors, 4096-bit stage latch 81,920-114,688; 2:1 mux stage 2,048 transistors per 512-bit operand, 16,384 per 4096-bit operand. The FDI crossing is mesochronous (phase-compensated forwarded-clock interface), not a two-flop synchronizer - stated explicitly in the section. Two disputes already recorded at Levels 2-3 need no new record: base-tile area 640 mm2 (deck) vs 646 mm2 (eeNews/ISSCC coverage), and the 512 B/clock load/store rate vs the deck diagram's '512 bit' text. Secondary source for the contract: eeNews Europe, 'Ponte Vecchio 3D supercomputer processor uses five process nodes', Feb 22, 2022 (ISSCC 2022).

records.quote: Arm 5th Generation GPUs introduce Deferred Vertex Shading (DVS). DVS means that the first phase, which we call the Binning phase, only computes and stores the primitive binning information. Full vertex shading is deferred to the second phase, which we call the Main phase.

records.current_value: No gate-level structure published; the Level-4 section states each primitive's gate-level form as textbook-standard construction and marks unpublished parameters as unpublished
records.fact: Level-4 decomposition scope boundary: Google publishes no gate-level structure for the SparseCore or the pod interconnect; the Level-4 text therefore decomposes every primitive as the generic textbook construction of that primitive, labelled standard construction, using only Google's published per-block geometry plus figures explicitly labelled as arithmetic derived from that geometry (spmem 6T cell totals 125,829,120 per SparseCore / 7,864,320 per bank / 503,316,480 per chip, arithmetic from the v4 2.5 MiB geometry v5p inherits; 15 adds in 4 levels for the 16-bank reduction; 15 2:1 muxes per bit for 16-way bank select; 75 2:1 muxes per bit across the five-consumer cross-channel fabric; 6 2:1 muxes per bit per router output, 42 per bit across the 7-port router; 136-entry OCS routing-table bound; 18,496 MEMS mirrors). The Palomar switching fabric and the circulator decompose to zero transistors — they are MEMS and optical devices, not gates — and the FIFO/queue primitive decomposes to zero gates in the optical path because the OCS is a circuit switch.
records.notes: Honesty record scoping the Level-4 boundary, per the run brief's expectation, following the Ada/RDNA3/Ponte Vecchio/Immortalis/PowerVR pattern. No verified record is drafted: no primary source read in this run publishes gate-level structure for the SparseCore or the pod interconnect, and the derived figures are labelled in-text as derived arithmetic, not published facts. records.fact: One nc_matmul is a LoadStationary + MultiplyMoving instruction pair
records.quote: For every nki.isa.nc_matmul(stationary, moving) call, TensorE executes two distinct Neuron ISA instructions: LoadStationary (short for LS): This instruction loads the stationary from SBUF and caches it in internal storage of TensorE. MultiplyMoving (short for MM): This instruction loads the moving from SBUF and multiplies moving across the pre-loaded stationary matrix from the previous LoadStationary instruction.

records.current_value: Four heterogeneous compute engines (Tensor, Vector, Scalar, GpSimd), each with its own sequencer; four independent instruction streams in parallel; synchronisation via atomic semaphores in hardware
records.fact: Four engines, own sequencers, hardware semaphore synchronisation
records.notes: Consistent with the wiki's existing verified fact on the four engines.
records.quote: A NeuronCore-v2 consists of four heterogeneous compute engines (Tensor, Vector, Scalar, and GpSimd), each designed to accelerate different types of operators in modern machine learning models. Each compute engine has its own sequencer, which is responsible for instruction fetch, decode, and issue. The four compute engines execute four independent instruction streams asynchronously in parallel. Explicit synchronization to satisfy data dependencies between engines is handled through atomic semaphores in hardware.

records.fact: Level-4 decomposition scope boundary: SambaNova publishes no gate-level structure for the SN40L; the Level-4 text therefore decomposes every primitive as the generic textbook construction of that primitive, labelled standard construction, using only SambaNova's published per-block geometry plus figures explicitly labelled as arithmetic derived from that geometry (PMU SRAM 520 MiB = 4,362,076,160 bits = 26,172,456,960 6T cell transistors per socket; 0.5 MiB per PMU = 4,194,304 bits = 25,165,824 cell transistors; per die 260 MiB = 2,181,038,080 bits = 13,086,228,480 cell transistors; PMU cells 25.7 percent of the deck's 102B transistors; 638 BF16 TFLOPS at a clock published only as under 2 GHz is at least 319,000 FLOPS per cycle per socket, about 307 per PCU per cycle; 638 TFLOPS from 102B transistors is about 6,255 BF16 FLOPS per second per transistor; 8x8 multiplier about 2,400 transistors; 32x32 INT32 multiplier about 35,712 transistors; FP32 mantissa multiplier about 20,256 transistors plus a 224-transistor exponent adder; 16-bit counter 768-896 transistors; 16-bit up/down counter 832-960 transistors; CAM cell 10 transistors; HBM/DDR 9x bandwidth gap). The tail's transcendental, RNG, stochastic-rounding and format-conversion functions are named only as candidate standard constructions, none asserted for the SN40L. No primitive decomposes to zero gates; two things are absent by design (no dynamic scheduler on the tile; no hardware cache in the three tiers). The deck's round '520 MB' reading would give 24,960,000,000 cell transistors, 4.6 percent lower than the MiB reading used.

records.fact: The ANE has no instruction set: neural ops arrive as a compiled chain of fixed-size task descriptors; the driver stages them and rings a doorbell
records.current_value: No CONV/MATMUL/RELU opcodes sent to hardware; Apple's compiler converts ops into task descriptors; driver loads the task to memory, sets TM_ADDR/TM_INFO, submits by ringing the doorbell (TM_PUSH)

source.title: Retrospectively Reverse-Engineering Apple's Neural Engine

records.quote: The driver never gives the ANE a CONV, MATMUL, or RELU opcode to run. All the neural operations have all already been compiled into a command stream of task descriptors (TDs), and the driver software simply loads the task to memory, sets the pointer to the opaque task blob via (TM_ADDR, TM_SIZE), and submits the staged task by ringing the doorbell (TM_PUSH).
records.notes: M1 generation, from the reverse-engineered Asahi Linux driver (ane/src/ane_tm.c). Each descriptor configures one pass through the fixed datapath; it does not encode arbitrary programs. Register pair corrected during the run: Yoon's prose shorthand says (TM_ADDR, TM_SIZE), but the driver code writes TM_ADDR and TM_INFO; TM_INFO[31:16] = descriptor_dwords - 1, TM_INFO[15:0] = descriptor_count.

records.fact: Level-4 gate/transistor boundary: NVIDIA publishes no gate-level structure, netlist or transistor count for Ada NVENC/NVDEC; all gate and transistor figures in the Level-4 decomposition are textbook-standard constructions of the named primitives, not claims about NVIDIA's silicon

source.title: NVENC Application Note (Video Codec SDK 13.0)

records.notes: The NVENC/NVDEC Application Notes (Video Codec SDK 13.0) describe pipeline stages, the API contract and codec features at block level; the codec specifications define the algorithms the silicon must implement. Neither source publishes gate-level structure, netlists, standard-cell descriptions or transistor counts for Ada's media engine, so every gate and transistor figure in the Level-4 decomposition is the generic textbook-standard construction of the named primitive (primer bottom layer), labelled as such in the wiki text. Arithmetic from published spec geometry (7 reference frames, 8-tap filters, 64x64 tile cap, 32 CDF update cap, 127 CABAC states, 15-bit CDF entries, renormalisation rule bits = 15 − FloorLog2(SymbolRange)) is labelled as arithmetic in the text; no new chip-specific number was introduced. Companion NVDEC boundary: NVDEC Application Note (Video Codec SDK 13.0).

records.notes: Apple's published media-engine material (ProRes White Paper Jan 2020; M1 Pro/Max, M2 Pro/Max, M3 Ultra newsroom releases; Apple Support MacBook Pro tech specs) describes the engine at block and codec-pipeline level only — engine counts, stream counts, codec menu — never its circuits; no netlist, standard-cell description or transistor count for any block is published. records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ does not use bracketed exposures; it captures frames of constant exposure set low enough to avoid blowing out highlights
records.notes: Constant exposure is the key design decision: frames at different exposures are harder to align, and large exposure variation can render local alignment impossible.
records.quote: First, we do not use bracketed exposures. Instead, we capture frames of constant exposure, which makes alignment more robust, and we set this exposure low enough to avoid blowing out highlights.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ starts from Bayer RAW frames, not the demosaicked RGB/YUV output of a hardware ISP
records.notes: RAW start gives more bits per pixel and circumvents the ISP's tone mapping and spatial denoising.
records.quote: Second, we begin from Bayer raw frames rather than the demosaicked RGB (or YUV) frames produced by hardware Image Signal Processors (ISPs) common on mobile platforms.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)
