records.fact: HDR+ alignment is a novel FFT-based algorithm and the merge is a hybrid 2D/3D Wiener filter
records.notes: The two algorithmic cores of the pipeline, named in the abstract.
records.quote: Third, we use a novel FFT-based alignment algorithm and a hybrid 2D/3D Wiener filter to denoise and merge the frames in a burst.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ runs in 4 seconds on device for a 12 Mpix image, with no user intervention
records.notes: The abstract's performance claim; Section 7 refines it to 2.5–4 seconds on a Snapdragon 810 depending on burst size.
records.quote: It runs in 4 seconds on device (for a 12 Mpix image), requires no user intervention, and ships on several mass-produced cell phones.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ input is a stream of Bayer RAW images at full sensor resolution (e.g. 12 Mpix) at up to 30 frames per second
records.notes: Figure 3 caption: the same RAW stream feeds both the viewfinder pipeline and the software burst pipeline.
records.quote: The input to both pipelines is a stream of Bayer mosaic (raw) images at full sensor resolution (for example, 12 Mpix) at up to 30 frames per second.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ viewfinder is 1.6 Mpix, updated at 15–30 frames per second
records.notes: The hardware-ISP viewfinder is the low-resolution preview; the software pipeline only runs at the shutter press.
records.quote: In our current implementation the viewfinder is 1.6 Mpix and is updated at 15–30 frames per second.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: At the shutter press the viewfinder suspends, a constant-exposure burst is captured and stored temporarily in main memory, then the software pipeline runs
records.notes: The burst lives in main memory between capture and merge — the memory cost behind the 104 Mpix figure.
records.quote: When the shutter is pressed, this pipeline suspends briefly, a burst of frames is captured at constant exposure, stored temporarily in main memory, and the software pipeline (bottom row) is activated.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ reference frame is the sharpest frame in a subset of the burst, chosen by a gradient metric on the green channel of the RAW input (lucky imaging)
records.notes: Reference selection defends against blur from hand and scene motion; the paper does no deblurring, so the reference's sharpness is the output's sharpness.
records.quote: To address blur induced by both hand and scene motion we choose the reference frame to be the sharpest frame in a subset of the burst, according to a simple metric based on gradients in the green channel of the raw input.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ reference frame is chosen from the first 3 frames in the burst, to minimise perceived shutter lag
records.notes: The first-3 constraint is a latency trade: a later frame could be sharper but would delay the shot.
records.quote: To minimize perceived shutter lag, we choose the reference frame from the first 3 frames in the burst.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ alignment runs at 24 milliseconds per Mpix on a mobile device
records.notes: Achieved with an FFT-based acceleration of the L2 alignment cost plus careful engineering.
records.quote: Our alignment algorithm runs at 24 milliseconds per Mpix on a mobile device.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ alignment is coarse-to-fine on four-level Gaussian pyramids of the RAW downsampled to gray
records.notes: Downsampling averages 2x2 blocks of Bayer RGGB samples, so alignment runs on 3 Mpix grayscale instead of 12 Mpix RAW; displacements are kept to multiples of 2 pixels so displaced Bayer samples keep coincident colours.
records.quote: To align an alternate frame to our reference frame, we perform a coarse-to-fine alignment on four-level Gaussian pyramids of the downsampled-to-gray raw input.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: At the finest pyramid level HDR+ tiles are 32x32 pixels with a maximum displacement of 64 pixels; the method supports displacements up to 169 pixels
records.notes: The 169-pixel figure is from the same Figure 5 caption: a hierarchical algorithm is essential because the large saturated-colour regions show large displacements.
records.quote: At the finest pyramid level (bottom right), tiles are 32 × 32 pixels and the maximum displacement is 64 pixels.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ merge typically uses 16x16 tiles from Bayer RAW colour planes, and 32x32 tiles for very dark scenes
records.notes: Larger tiles for very dark scenes because low-frequency noise can be objectionable there.
records.quote: Our method typically uses 16 × 16 tiles from color planes of Bayer raw input, but for very dark scenes, for which low-frequency noise can be objectionable, we use 32 × 32 tiles instead.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ merge pairs each reference tile with one tile from each alternate frame
records.notes: Pairwise (not 3D-DFT) merging: each alternate frame is evaluated independently, so one badly aligned frame cannot poison the whole merge.
records.quote: In our setting, each tile in the reference is merged with one tile taken from each of the alternate frames, corresponding to the result of our alignment.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ merge operates on tiles overlapped by half in each spatial dimension
records.notes: Half-overlap with a modified raised-cosine window avoids visible discontinuities at tile boundaries in the DFT domain.
records.quote: Our merge method operates on tiles overlapped by half in each spatial dimension.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ noise model: for a signal level x the noise variance is Ax + B, from the Poisson photon-counting process; A and B depend only on the shot's gain settings
records.notes: The signal-dependent noise model is what lets the Wiener filter tell alignment failure apart from noise.
records.quote: In particular, for a signal level of x, the noise variance σ² can be expressed as Ax + B, following from the Poisson-distributed physical process of photon counting.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ shipped on devices with 12–13 Mpix sensors, capturing bursts of up to 8 frames — as much as 104 Mpix stored and processed per output photograph
records.notes: The memory/compute cost of the burst bargain, stated in Section 7.
records.quote: Our system has shipped on devices having 12–13 Mpix sensors, on which we capture bursts of up to 8 frames. Thus, we may be required to store and process as much as 104 Mpix per output photograph.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: On a Snapdragon 810 a low-light HDR+ shot takes 4 seconds: 1 s capture, 500 ms alignment, 1,200 ms merge, 1,600 ms finish
records.notes: Measured on a Snapdragon 810 not subject to thermal throttling; a daylight shot takes 2.5 seconds (100 ms capture, 250 ms alignment, 580 ms merge, 1,600 ms finish). The finish stage dominates both cases.
records.quote: For a low light shot taking 4 seconds, this breaks down as 1 second to capture the frames, 500 ms for alignment, 1200 ms for merging, and 1600 ms for finishing.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ implements its own FFT in Halide, five times faster than FFTW on an ARM phone for the small DFTs in the pipeline
records.notes: The pipeline computes many small 2D real DFTs for align and merge, so a purpose-built FFT beat the general library.
records.quote: For the small DFTs in our pipeline, this implementation is five times faster than FFTW on an ARM-based mobile phone.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: HDR+ finish stage includes chroma denoising with an approximate bilateral filter — a sparse 3x3 tap nonlinear kernel applied in two passes in YUV
records.notes: One of the numbered finish steps in Section 6; colour correction uses a 3x3 matrix supplied by the ISP, and dynamic range compression, dehaze and global tone adjustment follow.
records.quote: Chroma denoising to reduce red and green splotches in dark areas of low-light images. For this we use an approximate bilateral filter, implemented using a sparse 3x3 tap nonlinear kernel applied in two passes in YUV.

source.title: Hasinoff et al., Burst photography for high dynamic range and low-light imaging on mobile cameras (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, ACM Transactions on Graphics 35(6), Article 192)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: Night Sight produces clean, sharp, colourful photographs in light as low as 0.3 lux
records.notes: At 0.3 lux human vision becomes monochromatic and indistinct; the system exceeds what the eye can see.
records.quote: In this paper we describe a system for capturing clean, sharp, colorful photographs in light as low as 0.3 lux, where human vision becomes monochromatic and indistinct.

source.title: Liba et al., Handheld Mobile Photography in Very Low Light (SIGGRAPH Asia 2019, ACM Transactions on Graphics 38(6), Article 164)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: Night Sight 'motion metering' estimates motion magnitudes (handshake or moving objects) to choose the frame count and per-frame exposure times that minimise both noise and motion blur
records.notes: Motion metering is the scheduling brain of Night Sight: it shapes the exposure schedule dynamically, slower exposures for still scenes, faster for scenes with motion.
records.quote: Our system employs “motion metering”, which uses an estimate of motion magnitudes (whether due to handshake or moving objects) to identify the number of frames and the per-frame exposure times that together minimize both noise and motion blur in a captured burst.

source.title: Liba et al., Handheld Mobile Photography in Very Low Light (SIGGRAPH Asia 2019, ACM Transactions on Graphics 38(6), Article 164)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: Night Sight captures and merges a burst of 6–13 frames
records.notes: Frame count is set by motion metering, not fixed: still scenes get more frames and longer exposures.
records.quote: Based on this exposure time, we capture and merge a burst of 6–13 frames (Section 3).

source.title: Liba et al., Handheld Mobile Photography in Very Low Light (SIGGRAPH Asia 2019, ACM Transactions on Graphics 38(6), Article 164)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: Night Sight total capture time is 1–6 seconds after the shutter press and processing time is under 2 seconds
records.notes: The 8-second maximum total (6 s capture + 2 s processing) is the hard budget in the requirements list.
records.quote: Total capture time is between 1 and 6 seconds after the shutter press and processing time is under 2 seconds.

source.title: Liba et al., Handheld Mobile Photography in Very Low Light (SIGGRAPH Asia 2019, ACM Transactions on Graphics 38(6), Article 164)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: In the Night Sight paper's 0.4 lux example, per-frame exposure was extended from 0.14 s to 0.33 s and the burst from 6 to 13 frames
records.notes: The concrete motion-metering payoff: low scene motion buys longer exposures and more frames, which is what removes the noise.
records.quote: Our pipeline (c) produces detailed images by selecting a longer exposure time due to the low scene motion (in this setting, extended from 0.14 s to 0.33 s), robustly aligning and merging a larger number of frames (13 frames instead of 6), and reproducing colors reliably by training a model for predicting the white balance gains specifically in low light.

source.title: Liba et al., Handheld Mobile Photography in Very Low Light (SIGGRAPH Asia 2019, ACM Transactions on Graphics 38(6), Article 164)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: Pre-capture motion metering estimates the flow field's magnitude in only 3 ms
records.notes: Motion metering runs on viewfinder frames before the shutter press, so the schedule is ready when the burst starts.
records.quote: Pre-capture motion metering is also efficient and can estimate the flow field’s magnitude in only 3 ms.

source.title: Liba et al., Handheld Mobile Photography in Very Low Light (SIGGRAPH Asia 2019, ACM Transactions on Graphics 38(6), Article 164)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: Night Sight uses a learning-based auto white balancing algorithm for accurate colour in low light
records.notes: Low-light scenes often have strongly coloured light sources; the learned colour-constancy model is trained and evaluated with a novel metric.
records.quote: To ensure accurate colors in such low light, we employ a learning-based auto white balancing algorithm.

source.title: Liba et al., Handheld Mobile Photography in Very Low Light (SIGGRAPH Asia 2019, ACM Transactions on Graphics 38(6), Article 164)

records.entry: Google Tensor G3 ISP + HDR+ Pipeline
records.fact: Night Sight tone mapping is inspired by illusionistic painting: increasing contrast, crushing shadows to black, surrounding the scene with darkness
records.notes: The tone mapping deliberately keeps the photograph reading as a dark scene instead of making night look like day.
records.quote: To prevent the photographs from looking like they were shot in daylight, we use tone mapping techniques inspired by illusionistic painting: increasing contrast, crushing shadows to black, and surrounding the scene with darkness.

source.title: Liba et al., Handheld Mobile Photography in Very Low Light (SIGGRAPH Asia 2019, ACM Transactions on Graphics 38(6), Article 164)
